description: Eval cases for the session-handoff skill. Tests structured handoff file creation, brain_store persistence, new agent spawning, grill answering, and verification. All cases from real April 4, 2026 handoff failures.

evals.prompt: My context is at 68% and I have 3 active agents working on a sprint. The user just said 'I'm going to sleep, wrap things up.' How do I hand off?
evals.expected_output: Should write a structured handoff file (NOT raw cmux text), brain_store the state, spawn a new agent, and set up monitoring. Should NOT just say 'goodnight' or end the session.

assertions.text: Writes a structured handoff file to docs.local/handoffs/ (not raw cmux text)
Includes agent state table with surfaces, tasks, and context %
brain_stores the handoff summary with appropriate tags
Spawns a new agent to continue the work
Does NOT just say 'goodnight' without handing off to a continuation agent

evals.prompt: I just spawned a new orcClaude to take over. It's asking: 'What's the current state? What should I focus on? What agents are running?' Should I tell the user to answer these questions?
evals.expected_output: Absolutely NOT — the OUTGOING agent must answer the grill questions from its own context. The user should never be a message relay.

assertions.text: Answers the new agent's questions directly (via send_input to its surface)
Does NOT tell the user to answer the grill questions
Does NOT wait passively for the user to relay information
Uses its own accumulated context to answer (it has the knowledge)

evals.prompt: I need to hand off but I've received 8 user corrections this session about routing, fabrication, and browser preferences. What goes in the handoff file?
evals.expected_output: All 8 corrections MUST be in the User Corrections section of the handoff file, with category, importance, and exact quotes. Without this, the new agent will repeat the same mistakes.

assertions.text: Includes a User Corrections section in the handoff file
Lists all 8 corrections with categories and exact user quotes
Does NOT omit corrections from the handoff (they're the most valuable transfer)
Includes importance levels for each correction

evals.prompt: The new agent is booted and I sent it the handoff file path. How do I know the handoff is actually complete?
evals.expected_output: Must verify: (1) new agent is actively working (read_screen shows tool calls), (2) monitoring is set up, (3) corrections are in BrainLayer (brain_search). Only THEN declare complete.

assertions.text: Checks that the new agent is actively working (read_screen, token count increasing)
Verifies monitoring is set up (CronCreate or /loop)
Verifies corrections are stored in BrainLayer (brain_search check)
Does NOT declare handoff complete without verification steps

evals.prompt: I'm at 72% context. Should I compact first or hand off directly?
evals.expected_output: At 72%, should hand off directly — NOT compact. Compaction loses 60-70% of context, and quality already degrades past 50%. A structured handoff to a fresh agent preserves more knowledge than a compaction.

assertions.text: Recommends handoff over compaction at 72% context
Does NOT recommend compacting at 72% (too late, loses too much)
Mentions that compaction loses 60-70% of context
Explains that structured handoff preserves more than compaction

evals.prompt: I want to hand off to a new session. Should I use 'orcClaude -s' or 'orcClaude -s -c' for the new agent?
evals.expected_output: For a TRUE handoff (new agent, fresh context): use 'orcClaude -s' (fresh session). '-c' continues the SAME session which defeats the purpose of a handoff. Only use '-c' if you want to resume your own session after a disconnect.

assertions.text: Recommends 'orcClaude -s' for a fresh handoff agent (not -c)
Explains that -c continues the same session (not a fresh start)
Does NOT confuse -s (skip-permissions) with -c (continue)

evals.prompt: The user told me to set up a /loop to monitor the new agent during handoff. I forgot. Now the user is reminding me for the second time. What happened?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this as a monitoring failure (same pattern as orc R4-R5). Should immediately set up the loop AND brain_store this as a correction (via /frustration-capture).

assertions.text: Immediately sets up the monitoring loop (CronCreate or /loop)
Recognizes this is a repeated instruction (user asked twice)
brain_stores this as a user correction via /frustration-capture
Does NOT make excuses for forgetting the loop
